text:
Anna: Quick heads-up — after the kernel-selector revert yesterday we're still seeing OOM spikes on canary for the checkout workload. I suspect the buffer-leasing layer + the kernel's workspace sizing.
Raj: Logs?
Anna: ```\n[serving-runtime] OOM: alloc 1.2GB failed at allocate_workspace(1024, logits_slab)\nstack: alloc.cc:342 lease_alloc()\n``` 
Megan: Is this only with long sequences or KV-cache-heavy traffic?
Anna: Mostly seq_len > 2048 and concurrent KV hits. Profiling shows logits buffers linger longer when KV miss paths trigger regeneration.
Luis: I ran nvprof and saw allocation churn at launch + per-batch:\n```\nGPU_ALLOC 0.5ms x 1200 calls\nGPU_FREE 0.2ms x 1180 calls\n``` 
Anna: @Raj can you dump a pprof for the allocator?
Raj: uploaded pprof to /tmp/allocator-pprof.pb — hot path is lease_reclaim under high batch concurrency. lease_timeout_ms default is 500 — could be too long.
Megan: We also bumped continuous-batching window to 15ms in canary last week. That can create bursty parallelism. Try batching-window-ms=5 for a test.
Anna: I reverted the kernel-selector but still got 2 OOMs overnight. Feels like scratchpad leasing isn't returning slots to the slab fast enough — freelist fragmentation.
Luis: One quick idea: eager-free logits slab on batch completion (return to head of freelist immediately). Cheap change, might reduce peak footprint.
Megan: Might lose reuse locality though — could hurt throughput. We should A/B it.
Raj: small experiment flags: --lease-eager-return=true, --slab-min-frag=64MB. Kicked a canary.
deploy-bot: Canary 5023 deployed to 10% traffic (region: us-west1).
Anna: After that deploy I saw ~3% increase in 99th latency for short seqs. Not huge but notable.
Luis: I profiled reclaim path — there's an extra memset for zeroing reclaimed buffers. Removing zeroing for non-sensitive scratchpads drops reclaim time by ~20%.
Megan: Also noticed KV routing change caused more cross-shard cache misses -> more full-token regenerations, which increases logits buffer lifetime. I added kv.cache_miss_rate and kv.eviction_rate to the console dashboards.
Anna: Proposed plan:\n1) revert eager-return on canary\n2) reduce batching-window to 5ms\n3) enable slab compact under low-pressure to fight fragmentation\n4) collect p99/oom counts and allocation traces for 24h
@Raj can you run the harness with seq distribution skewed to >2048 and KV-heavy traffic?
Raj: On it — I'll run a 24h load with skew and upload traces. Will also run with --lease-eager-return=false for comparison.
Megan: :thumbsup: logging notes in perf-run ticket PR-237.
Anna: Thanks — if OOMs persist next steps are per-model workspace caps and graceful fallback to quantized model variants to reduce peak workspace.
